name: PA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Chris Rabb's large fundraising and outside support edge
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 97%
model.rationale: This Philadelphia-based seat carries a roughly +40 Democratic partisan lean, and the Democratic nominee has outraised the independent challenger by more than 100-to-1 with substantial outside backing. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, so the forecast stays at Safe D with a margin near the district's fundamentals.
model.watch: A late independent surge or unusually low-turnout special dynamics are the only plausible paths to a closer result.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Dwight Evans (D) is not on the ballot.
Dennis Mahoney is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
Dwight Evans's retirement leaves a heavily Democratic Philadelphia seat open, with state Rep. Chris Rabb the heavy favorite against independent Dennis Mahoney. The district's partisan lean of roughly +40 Democratic makes a Republican-side upset nearly impossible in any normal environment, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive.

Rabb has raised about $1.3 million and benefits from roughly $1.6 million in outside support, while Mahoney has raised about $11,000 with no outside help. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability near 97%. The forecast expects a Democratic margin in the low 30s, consistent with the seat's fundamentals, with modest uncertainty because no general-election polling is available.
